title: Spinal Cord Stimulation: Trial and Permanent Implantation (Synthetic Health Plan — fictional policy)

sections.title: Synthetic Content Notice
sections.text: This document is a SYNTHETIC, fictional medical policy written for software testing and demonstration. It is not issued by any real health plan and must not be used for real coverage decisions.

sections.title: Coverage Criteria for a Trial
sections.text:
A spinal cord stimulator trial is considered medically necessary when ALL of the following are met:

1. Chronic neuropathic pain of the trunk or limbs (for example, persistent pain after spinal surgery or complex regional pain syndrome) has been present for at least 6 months.
2. The member has failed at least 6 months of multidisciplinary conservative treatment, including physical therapy, medication management, and when appropriate interventional procedures.
3. A psychological evaluation by a licensed mental health professional within the past 12 months has found no untreated psychiatric condition, active substance use disorder, or unrealistic expectations that would preclude a successful outcome.
4. Further surgical intervention is not indicated or the member is not a surgical candidate.
5. The member has no contraindication to implantation, such as active infection or uncorrected coagulopathy.

Permanent implantation is considered medically necessary only after a trial lasting at least 3 days that produced at least 50% reduction in pain and documented functional improvement or reduced analgesic use.

sections.title: Documentation Requirements
sections.text: Submit the pain history with onset date, a list of conservative treatments with dates and outcomes, the psychological evaluation report, the surgical opinion, and, for permanent implantation, the trial log documenting percent pain relief and functional change.

sections.title: Applicable Codes
sections.text: Procedure codes: 63650 (trial lead placement), 63685 (generator placement). Supporting diagnosis codes include G89.4 (chronic pain syndrome), M96.1 (postlaminectomy syndrome), G90.5 series (complex regional pain syndrome I).
